key_insight: Augmenting video MLLMs with per-frame learnable camera tokens and a lightweight pose regression head grounds frames in a shared 3D coordinate frame, enabling consistent, view-aware video understanding across time and viewpoints.
problem_solved: Current video multimodal LLMs treat frames as independent 2D images and lack camera-pose awareness, causing failures in spatial consistency, view-dependent reasoning, and long-range object permanence.
method: Introduce per-frame learnable camera tokens that represent each view and are tied to a shared scene coordinate frame.
Add a lightweight pose regression head trained with pose supervision to predict per-frame camera pose and condition multimodal transformer features.
Fuse pose-conditioned tokens into the existing video MLLM pipeline so the model learns view-aware, temporally consistent representations for downstream tasks.
impact: Provides a low-cost way to make video MLLMs 3D-aware, improving performance on view-dependent QA, localization and tracking while remaining compatible with existing transformer-based multimodal stacks—useful for robotics, AR, and scalable video understanding.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: video frames → per-frame camera tokens → pose regressor → pose-conditioned transformer
Scene illustration: multiple camera viewpoints with arrows showing a shared 3D coordinate frame and how tokens anchor frames to it
Qualitative examples: same object/scene from different angles with consistent model outputs (e.g., QA or tracking)
Performance chart: accuracy/consistency gains vs baseline MLLMs on view-dependent tasks
paper_authors: Jihan Yang, Zifan Zhao, Xichen Pan, Shusheng Yang, Junyi Zhang
